skill.name: api-route-design
skill.description: Design RESTful FastAPI routes with clear URL patterns, Pydantic validation, response models, status codes, pagination, filtering, and sorting.

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution and reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting and HTTP status documentation. No prompt injection, exfiltration, or executable command behavior was found. One semantic API safety issue remains because a complete endpoint example omits an explicit object-level authorization check.

remediation.issue: The fee detail route example does not show resource ownership or authorization enforcement.
remediation.suggestion: Update the example to load the fee in the current user scope or return 404/403 when the user cannot access it.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Object-Level Authorization in Example
semantic_findings.description: The complete fee detail endpoint accepts an authenticated user but fetches the fee by ID alone and returns it without showing an ownership or authorization check. This can teach broken object-level authorization if copied into an application.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example clearly includes an authenticated user parameter but does not use it when loading or returning the resource. Confidence is below very high because the undefined get_fee_by_id helper could enforce authorization internally.

content.value_statement: Designing REST API routes is hard when validation, status codes, pagination, and response models are inconsistent. This skill gives FastAPI patterns for predictable endpoints, Pydantic schemas, errors, filtering, sorting, and OpenAPI documentation.
actual_capabilities: Defines RESTful URL patterns for collection, resource, nested, create, update, patch, and delete endpoints.
Shows FastAPI request validation patterns for path parameters, query parameters, and Pydantic request bodies.
Recommends response models, error response shapes, and status codes for common API outcomes.
Provides complete endpoint examples with pagination, filtering, sorting, dependency injection, and OpenAPI summaries.
Includes a quality checklist for pagination, filters, sorting, response models, documentation, and error handling.
limitations: It focuses on REST APIs and does not cover GraphQL, WebSocket, or event-driven API design.
It provides design patterns but does not generate database models, migrations, or persistence logic by itself.
Security controls are examples only and must be adapted to each application authorization model.
The examples use FastAPI and Python conventions, so other frameworks may need translation.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Resource API
use_cases.description: Create consistent list, detail, create, update, patch, and delete routes before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Standardize Existing Endpoints
use_cases.description: Align status codes, response models, pagination, filters, and error responses across an existing FastAPI service.

use_cases.title: Review API Contracts
use_cases.description: Check proposed routes for clear resource naming, validation boundaries, response shapes, and OpenAPI documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Basic Routes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple resource API.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the api-route-design skill to design RESTful FastAPI routes for a resource named orders. Include list, detail, create, update, patch, and delete endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Add Validation Rules
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with request and query validation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the api-route-design skill to define FastAPI routes for invoices. Include Pydantic request models, path validation, pagination, filtering by status, and sorting rules.

prompt_templates.title: Review an API Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of existing endpoint design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the api-route-design skill to review these FastAPI endpoint names and response patterns. Identify inconsistent status codes, weak validation, and missing response models.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Secure Contract
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a production-ready route plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the api-route-design skill to design a production FastAPI contract for customer payments. Include authorization checks, pagination, filters, errors, status codes, and OpenAPI summaries.

output_examples.input: Design routes for a student fees resource.
output_examples.output: A route plan with collection and item endpoints, request models, response models, expected status codes, pagination, filters, and error responses.

output_examples.input: Review my FastAPI list endpoint for pagination and sorting.
output_examples.output: A concise review that flags missing limits, unclear sort fields, inconsistent response envelopes, and missing OpenAPI descriptions.

output_examples.input: Create an API contract for user notifications.
output_examples.output: A structured endpoint contract covering route names, methods, validation rules, response shapes, status codes, and authorization notes.

best_practices: Start with resource nouns, HTTP method semantics, and status codes before writing handler logic.
Define Pydantic request and response models for every public endpoint.
Document authorization, pagination, filters, sorting, and error responses as part of the route contract.
anti_patterns: Do not mix singular and plural resource names across related endpoints.
Do not return raw database objects without an explicit response model.
Do not copy example authorization patterns without enforcing object-level access rules.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets FastAPI and Python projects that use RESTful endpoint patterns.

faq.question: Can it design GraphQL APIs?
faq.answer: No. The skill is scoped to REST APIs and explicitly excludes GraphQL and WebSocket handlers.

faq.question: Does it create database CRUD code?
faq.answer: No. It can describe how routes call CRUD functions, but persistence implementation belongs in another layer.

faq.question: Does it cover validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for path parameters, query parameters, and Pydantic request bodies.

faq.question: Does it include pagination and sorting?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends skip and limit pagination, filter fields, sort fields, and sort direction controls.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
